agree.reason: The candid first-timer section and line-by-line budget would reassure this wary backer somewhat, but there is no refund promise, no fixed update schedule and not even the game's name, so someone who has already lost $85 is given little reason to trust it.

honest.reason: It doesn't say the 8.1 rating came mostly from people who played at the creator's own convention table, it makes up 'each session showed me something to fix', it calls the numbers checkable although shipping is approximate, and it says without support that 'most games' ask you to trust a prototype.

works_the_facts.reason: The 572 backers needed against 1,240 sign-ups is a sound, favourable calculation, and the budget split matches 10% fees, but the line that 1,500 copies is 'far more than the goal requires' is muddled, and the finished art and rules, the signed quote and the reviewer's launch-week video are all left out.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is an unsupported claim about 'most games on this platform', and the backer's real alternatives, which are not pledging or waiting for a retail copy, are never described.

qualification.reason: It gives a November 2027 delivery date but no consequence if that date is missed (the available refund after three months late is left out), and it promises updates 'at every stage' instead of the fortnightly schedule the creator can commit to.

objections.reason: It names the first-time-creator worry directly, but it answers it with a comparison to surveying instead of the refund guarantee and regular updates that actually address the fear of a project that never ships.

fit.reason: At about 500 words it is the right length and format for a pitch, but it never names the game (Lantern Winter) or the creator.
